'''Robert Eugene Wyatt''' is an emeritus [[Professor]] of [[Chemistry]] at the [[University of Texas at Austin]], Department of Chemistry and [[Biochemistry]].

== Work ==
Wyatt's work is focussed on [[theoretical chemistry]], including the [[quantum chemistry|quantum theory of chemical reactions]] and the theory of intramolecular [[energy transfer]]. His research has covered, among others, the [[De Broglie–Bohm theory#Quantum trajectory method|trajectory method of Bohmian mechanics]], based on work by [[Louis de Broglie]], [[Erwin Madelung]] and [[David Bohm]]. The method, found to be computationally more efficient{{cn|date=November 2019}} than methods that are based on a direct solution of the time-dependent [[Schrödinger equation]], has found wide acceptance{{weasel inline|date=November 2019}} by theoretical chemists.<ref>[http://www.tacc.utexas.edu/documents/13601/138850/Robert_Wyatts_New_Approach.pdf Robert Wyatt’s New Approach to Fundamental Problems in Quantum Chemistry] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160322123856/http://www.tacc.utexas.edu/documents/13601/138850/Robert_Wyatts_New_Approach.pdf |date=2016-03-22 }}, Texas Advanced Computing Center, Austin University of Texas (downloaded December 2, 2011)</ref>{{not in source|date=November 2019}}

In 2005 Wyatt published his book ''Quantum dynamics with trajectories'' with contributions by Corey J. Trahan.

Wyatt holds a W. T. Doherty professorship in chemistry at the Austin University of Texas.<ref>[http://www.cm.utexas.edu/endowments Endowed Chairs for Faculty Research and Teaching] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131024092756/http://www.cm.utexas.edu/endowments |date=2013-10-24 }}, Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry, University of Texas at Austin (downloaded December 2, 2011)</ref> An October 2007 edition of the [[Journal of Physical Chemistry A]] is a [[Festschrift]] dedicated to the work of Robert E. Wyatt and his group. Wyatt has been referred to as "the world's leading expert in quantum dynamics and theoretical chemistry".<ref>[http://www.iit.edu/csl/news/lykos_honors_robert_wyatt.shtml Professor Lykos Speaks at Conference Honoring Robert Wyatt], Illinois Institute of Technology (downloaded December 2, 2011)</ref>

He was elected a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] in 1989 ''"for fundamental contributions to the theoretical chemical dynamics, particularly quantum mechanical reactive scattering and laser-molecule energy transfer"'' <ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1989&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=APS|accessdate= 5 October 2020}} </ref>
